records.name: 215 Live Entertainment
records.summary: A Philadelphia performing arts group that teaches acting, dance, and voice to young people and adults, and stages shows about real social issues.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly class in acting, dance, or music, or audition for a youth company. Audiences can attend the group's events, such as an artist showcase and a murder mystery dinner.

schedule.text: Classes run once a week from January to December. Ages 6 to 13 take a 60 minute class, and ages 14 to 17 and adults take a 2 hour class. The Youth Acting Company rehearses on Saturday mornings, with some afternoon extensions.

cost.text: The Youth Acting Company charges a $30 registration fee on audition day and $60 a month in dues. The site does not list class prices.

first_step.how: Call 267-251-1156 to ask about a class or the Youth Acting Company, then book an audition appointment.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public with a phone line and a sign up path, but the site does not say whether a trial class is offered.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes meet once a week, and each student picks acting, dance, or music. The group describes its younger classes as building structure and confidence, and its older classes as building performance skills and preparing for work in the arts. The site does not list class prices, so ask before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come to confirm the class time, since the site does not list days or times for classes
Ask whether a trial class is possible before you pay the registration fee
Ask where classes are held, because the site does not give an address

records.notes: No dated events and no location, accessibility or language details on the site. The registration page and the youth company page each show a different email address (one on the group's own domain, others on gmail), so no email is recorded until the group confirms which is correct. The youth company auditions are for the 2026 season, which is the newest dated evidence, but no month is given, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The Rules and Regulations and Youth Dance Company pages were not read.

records.name: A Book a Day
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that gives books to children and families. It runs programs in medical settings, family events, and a children's writing and illustration program.
records.what_you_do: Come to an open family event, such as Children's Day or the Freedom to Learn fundraiser, or see an exhibit at The Study. The site does not describe how to volunteer, though it mentions past service days. Kids can enter the Philly Writers contests, but none was open when this was checked.

schedule.text: The group holds open events and exhibits a few times a year, each on its own date posted on the site. No weekly or monthly meeting is listed.

cost.text: Event prices are not listed on the site, which links to a donation page.

access.notes: Children's Day has included a quiet reflection room, according to the group's page.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on the group's site, then come to the next open event, such as the Freedom to Learn fundraiser at The Study on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 6 pm.
first_step.basis: Open events are listed with dates and places, and the newsletter and email address give a clear way in, though the site does not say how to get a ticket.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open events are for families and children. Past ones have included author meet and greets, a bookmaking activity, and a quiet reflection room. The site does not say how long an event runs or what it costs, so ask by email first.
first_visit_tips: Check the event listing on the site for the address before you go
Email the group with questions about cost, tickets, or access
Sign up for the newsletter so you hear about the next open event

records.notes: Fundraiser and exhibit dates are from the group's own page; the page shows the September 2026 posts as its newest. The Children's Day listing is August 22, 2026, and the MLK Day of Service listing is January 19, 2026 (past). No volunteer sign-up or phone number is on the site, and the volunteer and events pages returned 404. The Philly Writers page lists three past contests and no open one. The Puentes de Salud program name suggests Spanish language work, but the site does not confirm languages, so none are recorded. The mobile clinic wording from tier 1 was not seen on the pages read, so the summary was rewritten to match what the pages say. Facebook, Instagram and YouTube were not read.

records.name: A Novel Idea book clubs
records.summary: A bookstore on East Passyunk that runs book clubs on set dates, each built around a listed book.
records.what_you_do: Read the book listed for a club session, then attend on the set date. The site does not say whether sessions meet in the store or online.

schedule.text: Book clubs meet on dates the store posts on its site, usually in the evening. Check the site for the next date and book.

cost.text: Club titles are listed with prices from $17.95 to $30.00. The site does not say whether a price covers the book, a ticket, or a membership.

first_step.how: Get the book for the next listed club, then call the store at (267) 764-1202 to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Dated sessions and their books are listed, but the site does not say how to join or whether non-members can attend, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each session is built around one book on a set evening. The site does not say how long a session runs or who leads it. Ask the store before you come what a session costs and whether you need the book first.
first_visit_tips: Call the store before you come to confirm the date and whether the session is open to you
Get the listed book early so you can read it before the session
Ask whether the price covers the book, a ticket, or a membership

records.notes: The store's own site lists three sessions (a myth and legend club on October 8, 2026, a fiction club on October 29, 2026, and another myth and legend club on November 12, 2026), but no phone number, no join steps, and no statement on whether non-members can attend. The membership, book clubs and events sub pages returned 404. The phone number comes from a public directory listing and should be confirmed with the store. The open to public value is carried from tier 1 and the site does not confirm it. The Bookshop.org store page returned 403; a search result hinted at a monthly virtual club called Booklight PA, which was not verified and is not recorded.

records.name: Action Wellness Buddy Program
records.summary: Trained volunteers called buddies offer friendship, emotional support and some help with everyday tasks to people living with HIV, matched one to one with a client.
records.what_you_do: Visit or call a matched client on a regular basis, offer companionship, and help with small daily tasks. Buddies take part in monthly support meetings with other buddies.

schedule.text: Your visit schedule is set with the group after you apply and finish orientation. Orientation dates are posted on the volunteer page.

first_step.how: Fill out the volunteer application linked as Apply Now on the volunteer page, then attend the next virtual orientation listed on the site.
first_step.basis: A public application and an orientation come before any client match, so the way in is clear but not drop in.
first_step.what_to_expect: You start with an online application that asks for your contact details, two emergency contacts, and your date of birth, and it asks a yes or no question about criminal history. Orientation is a virtual meeting listed on the site, and a client match comes after it. The site does not give the length of orientation or a time commitment.
first_visit_tips: Be 18 or older and out of high school, which the application requires
Have two emergency contacts ready, with a name, phone number, and relationship for each
Call 215-981-0088 with questions before you apply

records.notes: Background check or clearance is not stated anywhere the site was read, so none is recorded. The application asks about criminal history with a required explanation if the answer is yes. The volunteer hub names Jamie Lefkowitz as the person to write for volunteer fit, and that email is recorded; the contact name carried from tier 1 is Mary Evelyn Torres. The hub mentions other agency volunteer roles (office support, special events) that were not read. Orientation length, time commitment, accessibility and languages are not stated. kids_ok is false because buddies must be 18 or older.

records.name: Actívate Stories
records.summary: A media arts group in the Philadelphia region that makes collaborative documentaries and runs a multimedia hub about arts work by Latinx, BIPOC, and immigrant artists. It also asks the public for archive material and works with videographers.
records.what_you_do: Send photos, videos, or audio of rumbas for the Philly Rumba archive call, or send a portfolio if you are a videographer. The events page lists screenings and gatherings, and some of them are free.

schedule.text: There is no weekly meeting listed. Calls, projects, and events are posted on the group's site as they come up.

cost.text: The site does not list prices for its events or calls, and it links to a donation page for money.

first_step.how: Send your material through the Dropbox request link on the group's Philly Rumba archive page, or email films@activatestories.org with questions.
first_step.basis: Open calls for material and portfolios each say how to send work, and public events list registration links, but the site does not describe a newcomer program or a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of what the group offers is a call for material or a public screening. If the team picks items from a personal collection for a film, it says it will offer an honorarium that you agree on first. Outdoor screenings in parks often ask you to register ahead.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page for the date, place, and whether you need to register
Ask about usage and credit before you send your material, since the call does not say
Email with questions before you send files so you know what format they want

records.notes: The events page lists 19 events from 2021 to 2027. The newest dated items are in October 2026 (a studio open house on October 9 and a media camp on October 3, the latter already past). Several events link to Eventbrite or Eventive for tickets, which were not read. The Germantown screening date on the events page is inconsistent (August 26 in one place, August 20 in another). The contact page has no email or phone, so the email comes from the opportunities and collaborate pages. The Philly Rumba archive call has no deadline. Online participation is set to true because archive material can be uploaded from anywhere; tier 1 had false. Partner groups named on the events and about pages are in leads_only.

records.name: Achilles International Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of Achilles International, which helps people with disabilities walk, run, and race. Members set goals and train with volunteer guide runners.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Saturday morning session at the fitness center, work toward a goal, and join group walks or rides. Volunteers can sign up as guide runners.

schedule.text: Athletes meet every Saturday at 9 am at the fitness center on the fourth floor of Liberty Place.

locations.label: Cigna Fitness Center, fourth floor, Liberty Place South Lobby

access.notes: The chapter welcomes people who are blind or have low vision, people who are deaf or hard of hearing, and people with other disabilities, including limb difference, cerebral palsy, and spinal cord injuries. The site also has an accessibility statement page.

first_step.how: Use the Join button on the chapter page to start athlete registration, then come to a Saturday 9 am session. To volunteer as a guide runner, email melissa@phillyachilles.com.
first_step.basis: The chapter welcomes new athletes with a clear registration step, but the page does not describe a beginner session or say whether a first visit can be drop in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Saturday sessions start at 9 am at the fitness center on the fourth floor of Liberty Place. The chapter describes its program as athletic activity plus social time, such as a weekly walk or ride in the park. Ask the chapter before you come how long a session lasts and whether there is a fee.
first_visit_tips: Email the chapter before you register to ask whether you can try a session first
Arrive a few minutes early to find the fourth floor fitness center
Wear comfortable clothes and bring water for a walk or ride
Tell the chapter ahead of time about any access needs so they can plan with you

records.notes: The Join and Volunteer buttons both open a third party registration login page, which was not used. The guide runner, volunteer and athlete sub pages returned 404. The chapter page's dated items are 2025 (a relay and a gala) and are organization wide with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out and status stays probably_active. No fee is stated. The chapter lists melissa@phillyachilles.com for athletes with disabilities and for guide runners; that address is in first_step, and the national info address is kept as the email. The menu mentions accessibility and language options but names no languages, so en is carried from tier 1. The accessibility statement page was not read.

records.name: ACLU of Pennsylvania
records.summary: The state chapter of the American Civil Liberties Union. It works on free speech, voting rights, immigrants' rights, LGBTQ equality, and fair treatment in the justice system, and it has volunteer and local chapter roles.
records.what_you_do: Sign up to volunteer through the group's form, join the Greater Philadelphia chapter, or sign up for the newsletter to hear about events and ways to take action. Volunteers can help with community outreach, direct action, lobbying elected officials, and behind the scenes support.

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteering or chapter activities. Donations are a separate choice.

first_step.how: Use the sign up link on the ACLU of Pennsylvania volunteer page, which opens an outside volunteer form, or email info@aclupa.org to ask about the Greater Philadelphia chapter.
first_step.basis: Volunteer and chapter sign up is open to people across the state, with a form and a chapter email, but the site gives no detail on a first step or an orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists four kinds of volunteer work: community outreach, direct action, lobbying elected officials, and behind the scenes support. It does not say how much time that takes, so ask the chapter what a typical month looks like before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter to hear about local events
Email info@aclupa.org with the county you live in to ask about the Greater Philadelphia chapter, which covers Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties
Ask about the next chapter event and whether a first timer can join it

records.notes: The volunteer sign up form is hosted by an outside organization. The chapter page gives no meeting schedule, dues or leadership, so no schedule is recorded. The volunteer page text was cut off, and the rest of it held only site navigation. The newest dated item is the October 8, 2026 news on the home page. Interests were added from the home page news items on a detention ruling, a gender-affirming care lawsuit, and felony murder and public defender items. The speakers bureau has its own request line and is not recorded. A guessed chapter sub page returned 404.
